title: Composition of finite equivariant generically etale covers with exact kernel invariants
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $V,W,T$ be normal integral projective finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $G,J,L$ be finite groups, with surjective homomorphisms $\sigma:J\twoheadrightarrow G$ and $\tau:L\twoheadrightarrow J$. Let $G$ act on $k,V$, let $J$ act on $W$ and on $k$ through $\sigma$, and let $L$ act on $T$ and on $k$ through $\sigma\tau$, all compatibly with the structure morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $a:W\to V$ and $c:T\to W$ be finite surjective morphisms, equivariant through $\sigma$ and $\tau$, respectively. Assume each is generically etale, meaning that $a$ is etale over a dense open subscheme of $V$ and $c$ is etale over a dense open subscheme of $W$. Identify $K=k(V)\subseteq M=k(W)\subseteq F=k(T)$ through their natural function-field embeddings. Suppose
$$ M^{\ker\sigma}=K,\qquad F^{\ker\tau}=M. $$
Then $a\circ c:T\to V$ is finite, surjective and etale over a dense open subscheme of $V$, is equivariant through the surjection $\sigma\circ\tau:L\twoheadrightarrow G$, and satisfies
$$ F^{\ker(\sigma\circ\tau)}=K. $$
The actions need not be faithful. In these formulas $E^P$ denotes the subfield of elements fixed by every member of the indicated subgroup $P$ acting on $E$; the actions on function fields are those induced by the scheme automorphisms. The terminal base $T$ retains its stated normal, integral, projective and finite-type properties over $k$.

Field, integral scheme, projectivity, finite type, finite morphism, surjectivity, etaleness, function field, field extensions, field towers, and open subschemes use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A group action here is a homomorphism to the group of scheme or field automorphisms, and a kernel is the subgroup mapped to the identity.

source.place: de Jong (1997), Remarks 2.3(iii), p.602, Situation 5.3, p.613, and Lemma 5.7 induction, p.615: composition of finite generically etale equivariant alterations. proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], $a\circ c$ is finite. It is surjective: for $v\in V$, choose $w\in W$ over $v$ and then $t\in T$ over $w$. Choose dense opens $V_0\subseteq V$ and $W_0\subseteq W$ over which $a$ and $c$, respectively, are etale.

source.place: Tags 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale); agent assembly of the finite-cover case of de Jong Remarks 2.3(iii).

proof.text: The fibre of $a$ over $\eta_V$ consists only of $\eta_W$. First $a(\eta_W)=\eta_V$: a closed subset of $V$ containing $a(\eta_W)$ has closed inverse image containing $\eta_W$, hence all of $W$, so surjectivity makes it all of $V$. On an affine neighborhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta_V$, finiteness gives $a^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $A,B$ domains. The ring map is integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]. The zero prime of $B$ contracts to the zero prime of $A$ by the generic-point equality. Any prime over $(0)$ contains $(0)$; [pqf-lem-incomparability] makes it equal to $(0)$.

source.place: Tag 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion), applied to the affine finite map, together with Morphisms Tag 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral); explicit generic-point argument by the worker.

proof.text: Set $Z=|W|\setminus |W_0|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $a(Z)$ is closed. The previous step and $\eta_W\in W_0$ imply $\eta_V\notin a(Z)$. Thus $U=V_0\setminus a(Z)$ is an open containing $\eta_V$, hence dense in $V$, and $a^{-1}(U)\subseteq W_0$.

source.place: Tags 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale); agent assembly of the finite-cover case of de Jong Remarks 2.3(iii).

proof.text: The restriction $a^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a base change of the etale morphism $a^{-1}(V_0)\to V_0$. Likewise $c^{-1}(a^{-1}(U))\to a^{-1}(U)$ is a base change of $c^{-1}(W_0)\to W_0$. They are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so their composite is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Its source is exactly $(a\circ c)^{-1}(U)$.

source.place: Tags 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale); agent assembly of the finite-cover case of de Jong Remarks 2.3(iii).

proof.text: For $l\in L$, equivariance gives $(a\circ c)\circ l=a\circ\tau(l)\circ c=\sigma(\tau(l))\circ(a\circ c)$. The homomorphism $\sigma\tau$ is surjective by choosing successive lifts. Pulling back germs in these same equivariance squares shows that the action of $l$ on $F$ restricts on $M$ to the action of $\tau(l)$, and on $K$ to the action of $\sigma\tau(l)$; these are the natural function-field embeddings specified in the hypotheses.

source.place: Agent proof of the equivariance and exact kernel-invariant assertion in the finite-cover composition strengthening of de Jong Remarks 2.3(iii), Situation 5.3 and Lemma 5.7 induction; uses only the stated action compatibility and two fixed-field equalities.

proof.text: Put $Q=\ker(\sigma\tau)$ and $N=\ker\tau$. If $x\in F^Q$, then $N\subseteq Q$ gives $x\in F^N=M$. For $j\in\ker\sigma$, choose $l\in L$ with $\tau(l)=j$. Then $l\in Q$, so compatibility from the preceding step gives $j(x)=l(x)=x$. Therefore $x\in M^{\ker\sigma}=K$. Conversely, if $x\in K=M^{\ker\sigma}$ and $l\in Q$, then $\tau(l)\in\ker\sigma$, so $l(x)=\tau(l)(x)=x$. This proves $F^Q=K$. No faithful action was used. The terminal scheme is the original $T$, so its normality, integrality, projectivity and finite-type properties are exactly the hypotheses.
